title: Leaders Who Tease Others Must Be Open to Being Teased Back
author: Admired Leadership
summary: The article examines teasing as a leadership tool, noting it can both signal closeness and soften indirect feedback, but that its meaning changes entirely depending on power balance. It catalogs the forms good-natured teasing can take, from nicknaming to joking accusations, and explains how leaders can use it to deliver criticism in a more palatable form. The core warning is that when a leader teases someone who doesn't feel able to tease back, the same behavior reads as ridicule rather than affection, and the target typically won't say so because of the power imbalance. The piece recommends leaders actively invite being teased back and make fun of themselves to keep the exchange genuinely mutual.
points: Teasing can carry indirect feedback, wrapping criticism in humor to make it easier for the recipient to accept.
The same teasing behavior reads as affection when mutual, but as ridicule when the power imbalance prevents the recipient from teasing back.
Because of that imbalance, targets rarely signal discomfort — they simply withdraw and avoid the leader's range, often without the leader noticing.
Good leaders keep teasing mutual by making fun of themselves and explicitly inviting others to tease them back.
quotes: Mutual teasing expresses closeness and signals that the parties are comfortable with each other and enjoy the mutual exchange of light humor.
Instead of expressing dissatisfaction or asking others to make a change, teasing offers the criticism wrapped in humor to make it easier to accept.
Without necessarily meaning to, leaders who tease individuals who do not feel comfortable teasing the leader back can project that they have a special status and enjoy an unequal power.
If they sense the leader may be intentionally trying to humiliate them, they will likely withdraw and stay out of target range whenever they can.
Good leaders engage more often like peers, reducing their status, so they can create the closeness they need to motivate and inspire others.
